summary.text: 本 is built from 木, a tree, and a mark at its lower part that indicates the root. The root sense is supported by transmitted explanations and literary examples; later recorded meanings include base, foundation, and source.

formation.text: Indicative: the lower mark identifies the root of the tree represented by 木. The construction is supported by transmitted and other analyses, although the earliest inscriptional form remains disputed.

components.text: 木 depicts the tree whose lower part the mark identifies. Here it gives the plant context; it is not a phonetic element.
一 is the lower mark indicating the tree’s base or root in one transmitted analysis. Another reading analyzes the mark as 丅, so its precise graphic identity is disputed.

history.text: The selected seal-script-style illustration is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact. Early inscriptional evidence is unsettled: a bronze example is listed in one record but not shown in another, and an oracle-bone precursor has been proposed but remains disputed. These accounts do not establish a secure sequence of graphic change.
The transmitted Shuowen explanation describes 木 with a mark below it. The mark is read as 一 in one text and as 丅 in another; this difference does not establish a chronological change in the graph.

uncertainties.text: The root-indicator construction is supported, but the earliest inscriptional form and date remain unresolved. The reported bronze graph's reading and meaning are unsettled, and the proposed oracle-bone precursor is disputed.
The cited texts and dictionary entries document several uses, but do not date or establish the precise pathways from root to abstract, documentary, or other meanings.

senses.text: The transmitted Shuowen explanation gives 本 the sense ‘root’; a cited Book of Odes passage uses it for a plant’s lower part or root. The passage’s exact composition date is not established.
A cited Zhuangzi passage records 本 for a tree trunk. Its first occurrence and precise relation to the root sense are undated.
Dictionary citations include base and foundation uses, such as the Analects phrase 君子務本，本立而道生. They do not date when this sense arose.
Source, cause, and basis are recorded meanings, but their precise development from root or foundation is undated.
Current definitions include root, origin, source, and basis; the list does not establish their chronology.

For Japanese ホン, one lexical account proposes that 本 meaning ‘original’ or ‘source’ came to refer first to an exemplar manuscript and then to books generally. This is a proposed Japanese word history, separate from the character’s graphic origin.

developments.text: Root and foundation are both documented; an extension from a plant’s base to a figurative basis is plausible, though the exact transition and chronology are not demonstrated.
Source and basis uses are recorded alongside foundation, but the precise development and dates are not shown.
For Japanese ホン, one account proposes a path from ‘original/source’ to an exemplar manuscript and then books generally; the dates of these steps are unresolved.

limitations.text: The cited literary passages and dictionary entries document uses but do not establish exact first-attestation dates or a complete chronology of semantic development.
The earliest archaeological attestation is unresolved, as is the reading of the reported bronze example.

items.period: Han Shuowen seal-script model; digital image uploaded 2016
items.caption: This seal-script-style form of 本 has a tree-like upper structure and a horizontal mark across its lower part. In the traditional analysis, 木 represents a tree and 一 marks its base, indicating the root. This is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact image.
items.alt: Bold black seal-script-style graph on white: a tree-like form with a horizontal stroke crossing its lower trunk.
items.selection_reason: It visibly illustrates the lower mark central to the traditional explanation of 本 as a root indicator, while its modern redraw status is made clear.
